items.title: The Remaining Two Right Efforts: Generating and Sustaining Wholesome States

items.zh: 於其未生一切善法，為令生故生欲者，謂於未得、未現在前所有善法，為欲令得、令現在前，發心希願，發起猛利求獲得欲、求現前欲，而現在前，是名於其未生一切善法，為令生故生欲。於其已生一切善法，為欲令住、令不忘失、令修圓滿生欲者，謂已獲得、已現在前所有善法，是名已生善法。於此善法已得不失、已得不退，依是說言：為欲令住。於此善法明了現前，無闇鈍性，依是說言：令不忘失。於此善法已得現前，數數修習，成滿究竟，依是說言：令修圓滿。於此善法發心希願，發起猛利求堅住欲、求不忘欲、求修滿欲，而現在前，是名於其已生一切善法，為欲令住、令不忘失、令修圓滿生欲。策勵者，為於已得令現前故。發勤精進者，為於未得令其得故。
items.en: Generating the aspiration, for unarisen wholesome states, that they arise, is generating an intense wish to obtain them and to bring them before the mind. Generating the aspiration, for arisen wholesome states, that they abide, not be forgotten, and be brought to completion: that they be obtained and not lost, obtained and not regressed from, is called "that they abide"; that they remain clear and present, free of any dullness, is called "that they not be forgotten"; that, already present, they be practised again and again until brought to final completion, is called "that they be brought to completion." Self-spurring is for the sake of bringing what has already been obtained before the mind; diligent effort is for the sake of obtaining what has not yet been obtained.

items.zh: 又策勵者，於已生善為欲令住、令不忘故。發勤精進者，令修滿故。又於下品、中品善法，未生令生，生已令住、令不忘失，是名策勵。於上品善法，未生令生，生已乃至令修圓滿，是名發勤精進。

items.title: Spurring the Mind and Sustaining It — Balancing Sinking and Agitation

items.zh: 言策心者，謂若心於修奢摩他一境性中正勤方便，於諸未生惡不善法，為令不生；廣說乃至於其已生一切善法，為欲令住、令不忘失、令修圓滿。由是因緣，其心於內極略下劣、或恐下劣，觀見是已，爾時隨取一種淨妙舉相，慇懃策勵、慶悅其心。是名策心。云何持心？謂修舉時，其心掉動、或恐掉動，觀見是已，爾時還復於內略攝其心，修奢摩他。是名持心。
items.en: Spurring the mind is: when the mind, diligently applying itself within the one-pointedness of calm-abiding practice … becomes, or threatens to become, extremely contracted and low within — upon observing this, one then takes up one of the pure, excellent images used for lifting the mind, vigorously spurring and gladdening it. This is spurring the mind. What is sustaining the mind? When, during the practice of lifting, the mind becomes, or threatens to become, agitated — upon observing this, one then returns the mind, contracting it inward again, to the practice of calm-abiding. This is sustaining the mind.

items.title: Section: Two Further Names — the Four Right Victories and the Four Right Cuttings

items.zh: 如是四種，亦名正勝。謂於黑品諸法，其未生者為令不生，其已生者為令斷滅，生欲、策勵、發勤、精進、策心、持心，是二正勝。於白品諸法、其未生者為欲令生，如前黑品廣說、應知是二正勝。如是四種，亦名正斷。一名律儀斷。謂於已生惡不善法，為令斷故，生欲、策勵，乃至廣說。二名斷斷。謂於未生惡不善法，為不生故，生欲、策勵，乃至廣說。由於已生惡不善事，應修律儀，令其斷滅，不應忍受。由是因緣，名律儀斷。於其未生惡不善事，為欲令彼不現行斷，為欲令彼不現前斷，為斷故斷，故名斷斷。
items.en: These same four are also called the four right victories: regarding dark states, preventing what has not arisen and ending what has — this is two right victories; regarding bright states, generating what has not arisen and sustaining what has, exactly as explained for dark states — this is the other two right victories. These same four are also called the four right cuttings. The first is called discipline-cutting: regarding unwholesome states already arisen, generating the aspiration and effort to end them. The second is called cutting-upon-cutting: regarding unwholesome states not yet arisen, generating the aspiration and effort that they not arise. Because one should, through discipline, end what unwholesome has already arisen rather than tolerate it, this is called discipline-cutting. Regarding what unwholesome has not yet arisen: cutting off its coming to manifest, cutting off its coming to appear, cutting for the very sake of cutting — hence it is called cutting-upon-cutting.

items.title: Section: Cultivation-Cutting and Protection-Cutting Close the Four Right Efforts

items.zh: 三名修斷。謂於未生一切善法，為令生故，廣說乃至策心、持心。由於善法數修數習，先所未得能令現前，能有所斷，故名修斷。四名防護斷。謂於已生一切善法，為欲令住，廣說乃至策心，持心。由於已得、已現在前諸善法中，遠離放逸，修不放逸，能令善法住不忘失，修習圓滿，防護已生所有善法，能有所斷故，名防護斷。如是廣辨四正斷已，復云何知此中略義？謂為顯示於黑白品捨取事中，增上意樂圓滿及加行圓滿，是故宣說四種正斷。
items.en: The third is called cultivation-cutting: regarding all wholesome states not yet arisen, generating them through repeated cultivation and practice, bringing what was previously ungained before the mind, and thereby cutting off what obstructed it. The fourth is called protection-cutting: regarding all wholesome states already arisen, remaining free of negligence so that they abide, are not forgotten, and are protected from loss — thereby likewise cutting off what would obstruct them. All of this is taught in order to display, with respect to what should be abandoned among dark states and what should be taken up among bright ones, the perfection of aspiration and the perfection of application — this is why the four right efforts are taught.

items.zh: 當知此中，由生欲故，增上意樂圓滿；由自策勵、發勤精進、策心、持心故，加行圓滿。修瑜伽師唯有爾所正應作事。謂為斷滅所應斷事，及為獲得所應得事，先當生起希願樂欲；為斷諸纏，復應時時正勤修習止、舉、捨相；為斷諸纏及隨眠故，更應修集對治善法。為現如是一切所作，說四正勝及四正斷。是名略義。

blocks.text: The last two right efforts, and their other names.

For wholesome states not yet arisen, "an intense wish to obtain them and bring them before the mind". For those arisen: "that they abide" ("obtained and not lost"), "that they not be forgotten" ("clear and present, free of dullness"), that they be completed and increased. Master Cháng Bǎi: forgetting here means losing clarity.

When the mind in calm "becomes, or threatens to become, extremely contracted and low", "one takes up a pure, excellent image used for lifting the mind, spurring and gladdening it". When it "becomes, or threatens to become, agitated", one returns it to inner calm. This is the practical balance of every meditation session.

The four are also called the four **right victories**: for dark states, preventing and ending; for bright states, generating and sustaining. And the four **right cuttings**: cutting by restraint, cutting by abandonment, cutting by cultivation, cutting by protection. Master Cháng Bǎi and Venerable Miào Jìng differ slightly on the first two.
"Cultivation-cutting: generating wholesome states not yet arisen through repeated cultivation." "Protection-cutting: guarding those already arisen."

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate "abide, not be forgotten, be brought to completion"?
quiz.why: "That they be obtained and not lost, obtained and not regressed from, is called 'that they abide.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: abiding, not being forgotten, and being brought to completion are three stages.

quiz.q: "Not forgotten" means clear and free of dullness. What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: one skilled in foulness contemplation sees a beauty and the contemplation arises at once — strong mindfulness
quiz.why: "That they remain clear and present, free of any dullness, is called 'that they not be forgotten.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: for instance, one already able to practise foulness contemplation meets a beautiful woman and the contemplation arises at once — mindfulness is strong, with no dullness.

quiz.q: What is spurring the mind, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the "pure, excellent image" is?
options: when the mind sinks, take a lifting image to rouse and gladden it — one of the six recollections
quiz.why: "One then takes up one of the pure, excellent images used for lifting the mind, vigorously spurring and gladdening it." Master Cháng Bǎi: at that time take one of the pure images of the six recollections and diligently lift the mind.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe sustaining the mind in practice?
options: stop observing, switch to calm, narrow the object and gather the mind
quiz.why: "When, during the practice of lifting, the mind becomes, or threatens to become, agitated — one then returns the mind, contracting it inward again, to the practice of calm-abiding." Master Cháng Bǎi: stop observing, switch to calm, shrink the object, and gather the mind.

quiz.q: The note splits "cutting-upon-cutting" into three angles. What do the lectures say?
options: only two: one cuts manifestation, the other seeds; one cuts seeds for the sake of cutting manifestation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one keeps affliction from manifesting, the other keeps it from appearing — Venerable Miào Jìng explains "not appearing" as cutting the seeds. Venerable Miào Jìng: "cutting for the sake of cutting" — to cut manifest evil, one cuts the seeds.

quiz.q: What is cultivation-cutting, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "cutting through cultivation"?
options: by repeated cultivation the unattained appears; obstacles cut, the good arises
quiz.why: "Generating them through repeated cultivation and practice, bringing what was previously ungained before the mind, and thereby cutting off what obstructed it." Venerable Miào Jìng: all obstructions are cut away and the wholesome arises — cutting through cultivation.
